data.summary: This response reports 1 test and 2 aggregations from 800 of 800 records; 0 of 1 inferential finding shows evidence at its alpha.
sentences: This response reports 1 test and 2 aggregations from 800 of 800 records; 0 of 1 inferential finding shows evidence at its alpha.
Test 1 (TEST_T) on `spend` split by `arm` finds no evidence of a difference at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.0673). Its effect size `cohens_d` is 0.131, very small by the convention of Cohen (1988).
Aggregation 1 `total_spend` runs the operator smart defaults chose on `spend`. Its value is 5.35e+04. It read 779 rows and left out 21 with no value.
Aggregation 2 `avg_spend` runs AGG_AVERAGE on `spend`. Average of a numeric field, over all rows or per group. Its value is 68.6. It read 779 rows and left out 21 with no value.
The run read 800 records; 800 passed the filters and 21 were left out for a missing value.
caveats: TEST_T: Rows are independent of each other, within and across groups.
TEST_T: The two-group version uses Welch's correction, so the groups need not have equal variances.
TEST_T: The average is roughly normally distributed: safe for large groups, risky for small skewed ones.
TEST_T: The p-value is two-sided: it looks for a difference in either direction.
